question: A 42-year-old woman is newly diagnosed with seropositive (anti-CCP positive) rheumatoid arthritis. She has active synovitis of 8 joints and radiological evidence of early erosions. Her physician prescribes a DMARD. Which of the following is the recommended FIRST-LINE DMARD for RA, and why is it preferred?

answers.text: Hydroxychloroquine — low side-effect profile and oral administration make it the safest first-line choice for all RA patients.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Hydroxychloroquine is a weak DMARD used for mild RA or SLE, not for patients with active synovitis and erosions. It lacks the anti-erosive potency required here. Methotrexate is the standard anchor DMARD.

answers.text: Methotrexate — most evidence for preventing joint erosion, fastest-acting among conventional DMARDs, and serves as the anchor for combination therapy and biologic add-on.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Methotrexate (MTX) is the global first-line DMARD for RA with active disease and erosions. It is the most evidence-backed conventional DMARD for halting radiological progression, has a well-characterised safety profile with folic acid supplementation, and is the required backbone for all biologic combinations (e.g., MTX + anti-TNF). All DMARDs treat inflammation; only MTX-level agents prevent structural damage in seropositive erosive RA.

answers.text: Sulfasalazine — the most potent DMARD with proven anti-erosive efficacy superior to methotrexate.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Sulfasalazine is a conventional DMARD used in RA and AS but is not more potent than methotrexate. In patients with active seropositive RA and erosions, methotrexate is preferred as the anchor agent due to superior anti-erosive evidence.

answers.text: Adalimumab (anti-TNF biologic) — biologics are now first-line because they work faster than conventional DMARDs.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Anti-TNF biologics (e.g., adalimumab, etanercept) are reserved for DMARD-refractory RA (typically inadequate response to MTX ± 1–2 other conventional DMARDs). They are not first-line at diagnosis due to cost, infection risk, and the fact that MTX alone achieves adequate control in many patients.

overallFeedback.feedback: Management hierarchy: NSAIDs (symptom relief only) → conventional DMARDs with MTX as first-line anchor (anti-erosive, backbone for combination therapy) → biologics (anti-TNF/IL-6/JAK inhibitors) for MTX-refractory disease.
Correct. MTX = anchor first-line DMARD for RA. NSAIDs relieve symptoms only; MTX modifies the disease and prevents erosions. Biologics are added when MTX fails.
